data.name: Ghiyaath
data.gender_notes: Ghiyaath is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root g-h-y, meaning 'to help'. In Islamic contexts, Ghiyaath refers to the one who provides help and support, often in times of need or distress. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) is known as the Ghifar (the Helper), as he helps his followers reach paradise. The name Ghiyaath carries the meaning “Help, Aid, Support” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ghiyaath usually hope their child will grow to embody help, aid, support and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of compassion, kindness, and support.
data.etymology: Ghiyaath belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Help, Aid, Support.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ghiyaath total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

He was a patron of the arts and sciences, and during his reign, he oversaw the construction of several notable structures including the Citadel of Cairo and the Mosque of Muhammad Ali. He is also known for his military campaigns against the Crusaders and the Mongols.
